thread:
Carmen H: heads-up — we need a quick plan for handling preemptible evictions for KV-prefix streaming requests. today a couple of streams dropped during spot churn, causing token gaps and client retries. thinking graceful drain + ttl-aware requeue + sticky fallback to on-demand for tails.

Raj P: agree. i think the simplest is a short requeue window that preserves prefix KV checkpoints. if we requeue within Xs we can resume without client-visible replay.

Lee S: +1. proposal: emit a checkpoint to redis right before drain, include seq/token, then atomically switch stream source. fallback path reads checkpoint and resumes.

Maya T: curious on cost—if we fall back to on-demand for tails how do we cap spend? maybe only for requests > 2s remaining or p99 latency risk.

Carmen H: good call. idea: hybrid policy = prefer preemptible, but if remaining tokens > threshold OR remaining latency SLO at risk, route to on-demand pool for that request.

infra-bot: [notice] preemptible-gpu-pool-us-west2 reported 12% node churn in last 5m — spike in reclaim events.

Raj P: here is a rough config prototype:
```
requeue:
  window_seconds: 10
  max_attempts: 3
  backoff_ms: 250
kv_cutover:
  checkpoint_prefix: "kv/cutover/{shard}"
  checkpoint_ttl_seconds: 45
fallback_policy:
  on_demand_threshold_tokens: 512
  on_demand_max_minute_pct: 0.8
```

Lee S: we should also add a token-bridge header in the stream so downstream can detect cutover and request resume idempotently. example header: `x-rwstream-resume-id`

Maya T: can ops add a guardrail metric: %requests switched to on-demand per minute and a hard cap alert at 5% of baseline spend? if that flips we rollback.

Carmen H: ops: @infra-bot can we surface a realtime metric for "cutover-resume-rate" and an alert if fallback_percent > 3% over 5m?

infra-bot: ack — creating metric "cutover.resume_rate" and alert rule with 3% threshold. (will post rule id shortly)

Raj P: rollout plan: feature flag gated, start with 10% traffic in staging -> soak for 24h -> 10% in canary -> 1h/4h checks for resume correctness -> ramp.

Lee S: add a tiny client-side backoff too. serverside requeue should be best-effort: clients must be idempotent for duplicate tokens.

Carmen H: action items:
- Raj: implement server requeue + checkpoint emission (ETA 48h)
- Lee: add header + resume semantics to client lib (ETA 72h)
- Maya/ops: create metric + alert, and cost cap guardrail (ETA 24h)
- infra-bot/deploy-bot: prepare a rollback playbook and a quick route toggle for on-demand pool (owner: infra)

deploy-bot: recent logs from one affected worker:
```
2026-03-17T18:12:07Z worker-23 reclaim-signal received
2026-03-17T18:12:07Z emitted checkpoint kv/cutover/shard-7 -> ok
2026-03-17T18:12:07Z draining connections (grace 8s)
2026-03-17T18:12:15Z connection closed before resume
2026-03-17T18:12:17Z request requeued to pool:on-demand
```

Maya T: that log shows checkpoint emission works but we still lost one resume. need to harden the pre-shutdown flush. maybe bump grace to 12s or ensure checkpoint write is synced before signaling drain.

Raj P: agree. will change flush to fsync-like barrier and bump grace to 12s behind a flag.

Carmen H: ok. i'll open the feature-flag PR and the rollout doc. keep replies short here and ping if you need sync. :thumbsup:

Lee S: noted. i'll update client lib and add tests for duplicate resume ids.

Maya T: ops will watch alerts during canary and have kill-switch ready.

infra-bot: metric rule created: id=mr-81243 "cutover.resume_rate" alert on >3% for 5m.

Carmen H: thanks team — will follow up with the PR links and the playbook.
